ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Categorical quality head on Qwen2.5-7B anchored by 2000 absolute ratings
PROPOSAL: Train Qwen2.5-7B with a head that outputs a categorical distribution over 5 absolute quality levels, using the Bradley-Terry loss on 60000 Skywork-Reward-Preference pairs together with a cross-entropy term on 2000 absolute ratings taken from HelpSteer2 attributes. Use the expected level as the score, the entropy as confidence and one fixed threshold as the acceptance rule. Evaluate pairwise accuracy on RewardBench and RM-Bench, calibration error on 500 held-out rated responses, and Best-of-16 gains on 300 AlpacaEval prompts.
CONTROLS: A scalar Bradley-Terry model on the same backbone and pairs, the same model without the rating term, a version with 500 ratings instead of 2000, and a threshold fitted on the validation split.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Pairwise accuracy should stay within 1 point of the scalar model while calibration error is roughly halved. The distribution may fail to separate good from bad responses on code prompts, where the HelpSteer2 ratings are sparse.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scalar reward model on Llama-3.1-70B with low-rank adapters, retrained with 5 seeds
PROPOSAL: Train Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct with low-rank adapters and a scalar head under the Bradley-Terry loss on the 7000 pairs of HelpSteer2-Preference, then retrain with 5 different seeds and average the weights of the runs. Score by the scalar output, take the score variance over the 5 runs as confidence and fix one threshold from the validation split. Evaluate pairwise accuracy on RewardBench, calibration error on 500 held-out rated responses, and Best-of-16 gains on 300 AlpacaEval prompts.
CONTROLS: Single-seed training with the same adapters, a 7B backbone trained on the same pairs, adapters of rank 8 instead of 64, and a threshold chosen by the Youden index.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: The 5-run ensemble should lift pairwise accuracy by about 1 point over one seed and give calibration error near 0.08. The variance-based confidence may fail to track annotator disagreement, since all runs see the same labels.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Critique-then-score generative reward model trained with reinforcement learning on Qwen3-8B
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune Qwen3-8B so that it writes a short critique and then emits a score token from 1 to 10 for a single response. Train for 2 epochs at learning rate 1e-5 with reinforcement learning on 40000 preference pairs, rewarding the policy when the chosen response scores above the rejected one, and read the probability over the 10 score tokens as a distribution whose entropy gives confidence. Evaluate on RewardBench and RM-Bench, and on Best-of-8 selection for 200 MATH-500 problems, scoring the 8 candidates independently.
CONTROLS: A Bradley-Terry model on the same backbone and pairs, the same recipe with the critique removed, a pairwise generative judge trained on the same pairs, and a variant that samples 4 critiques before averaging.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The scorer should come within 1 point of the Bradley-Terry model on RewardBench and beat it on Best-of-8 selection by about 2 points. It may fail when critiques are long, since a score token read after a wrong argument inherits its error.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scaling study of distributional heads over five backbones and four preference sets
PROPOSAL: Train a categorical quality head and a scalar head on 5 backbones, Qwen2.5-0.5B, 1.5B, 3B, 7B and 14B, using the Bradley-Terry loss on 4 preference sets: Skywork-Reward-Preference, HelpSteer2-Preference, UltraFeedback and Nectar, with 3 seeds per setting. Add absolute ratings to the distributional runs. Evaluate pairwise accuracy on RewardBench, calibration error on 500 rated responses and agreement with annotator vote splits, then fit power laws of each metric against parameter count.
CONTROLS: Scalar heads on the same backbones and sets, distributional heads without the rating term, models trained on the union of the 4 sets, and single-seed runs of the configurations.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Calibration error should fall faster with scale for the distributional head than for the scalar head, with exponents about 0.1 apart. The fit may fail if the 4 sets differ so much in label noise that set effects swamp the scale trend.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibration layer for a frozen reward model adapted to role-play dialogue
PROPOSAL: Freeze Skywork-Reward-Llama-3.1-8B and train a small monotone mapping from its scalar score to a 1 to 5 absolute rating, using 300 rated role-play replies, so that ranking is untouched by construction, fitted with 200 steps at batch size 32. Add a prompt-conditioned shift fitted on the same 300 ratings to absorb the domain difference. Evaluate rating error on 400 held-out rated replies, the accuracy of one fixed acceptance threshold, and pairwise accuracy on 1000 role-play preference pairs before and after the mapping.
CONTROLS: The frozen model with a global threshold from the source domain, isotonic regression alone, the full model fine-tuned on the 300 ratings, and the mapping fitted on 100 ratings.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Pairwise accuracy should be unchanged to within 0.2 points and rating error should fall by about 30 percent against the source threshold. The prompt-conditioned shift may fail to generalize to character types absent from the 300 ratings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Full fine-tuning of Skywork-Reward-Gemma-2-27B on role-play ratings, retrained 5 times
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune Skywork-Reward-Gemma-2-27B with low-rank adapters on 3000 rated role-play replies with a regression loss on the 1 to 5 rating plus the Bradley-Terry loss on 6000 role-play pairs, then retrain with 5 different seeds. Fit the acceptance threshold on the validation split of the run. Evaluate rating error on 400 held-out rated replies, the accuracy of the fixed threshold, and pairwise accuracy on 1000 role-play preference pairs before and after adaptation.
CONTROLS: The frozen model with a global threshold from the source domain, a 7B reward model trained with the same recipe, training on pairs only, and the same recipe on 1000 ratings.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Rating error should fall by about 40 percent against the source threshold with pairwise accuracy within 0.5 points of the frozen model. Large-model adaptation may fail through drift in ranking, since all weights of the adapters move to fit the ratings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reinforcement-trained categorical reward model on Qwen2.5-32B with annotator-vote targets
PROPOSAL: Train Qwen2.5-32B to output a categorical distribution over 7 quality levels with reinforcement learning on 80000 preference pairs, where the target for a pair is the annotator vote fraction when available and 0.5 and 1.0 otherwise. Combine the ranking reward with a calibration reward on 5000 absolute ratings from 3 domains, and run 2 epochs. Evaluate RewardBench, RM-Bench and JudgeBench, calibration error per domain, and Best-of-32 gains on 500 prompts from MATH-500 and LiveCodeBench, then ablate the 3 reward terms one at a time.
CONTROLS: A Bradley-Terry model and a pairwise generative judge on the same backbone and pairs, the model trained on hard labels only, the model without the calibration reward, and one retraining with a different seed.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: Calibration error should fall by about 40 percent against hard-label training with ranking accuracy within 1 point. The method may fail on code, where the vote fractions are near 0.5 for most pairs and carry little signal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Loss-weight sweep for a distributional reward model on Qwen2.5-14B over 8 settings
PROPOSAL: Train a categorical quality head on Qwen2.5-14B with the Bradley-Terry loss on 80000 preference pairs and a rating loss on 5000 absolute ratings, sweeping the rating-loss weight over 8 values from 0.01 to 10 and retraining the settings with 3 random starts. Evaluate RewardBench, RM-Bench and JudgeBench, calibration error on 500 rated responses from 3 domains, and Best-of-32 gains on 500 prompts from MATH-500 and LiveCodeBench, then report the best weight per domain and per metric.
CONTROLS: A Bradley-Terry model on the same backbone and pairs, the rating loss alone, the sweep winner retrained with 5 new seeds, and a model trained on ratings only for 1 epoch.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: A weight between 0.1 and 1 should give the best trade-off, losing under 1 point of ranking accuracy while cutting calibration error by about 35 percent. The sweep may fail to show a stable optimum if seed variance exceeds the difference between neighbouring weights.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Threshold transfer of public reward models across chat, math and code
PROPOSAL: Score 3000 responses per domain from chat, math and code with Skywork-Reward-V2-Llama-3.1-8B and ArmoRM, no training involved. Define good as an absolute rating of 4 or more on HelpSteer2 attributes for chat and as a verified correct answer for math and code. Fit one score threshold on chat and measure its accuracy and AUROC on the other 2 domains, then compare with a threshold fitted per domain. Use 3 random splits of 1000 responses for the threshold fit. Report how far scores drift between domains, using the score distributions of correct responses.
CONTROLS: A threshold fitted per domain, a random-score baseline, rank-normalized scores before thresholding, and bootstrap resampling of 200 draws for the intervals.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The chat threshold should lose about 15 points of accuracy on math and code against domain-specific ones. The comparison may fail to be clear if the two models differ in score range so much that per-model effects dominate.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Threshold stability of Skywork-Reward-Gemma-2-27B on math with repeated scoring passes
PROPOSAL: Score 3000 math responses with Skywork-Reward-Gemma-2-27B under 5 scoring passes that use dropout in the value head with different seeds, no training involved. Define good as a verified correct answer on MATH-500 and GSM8K solutions sampled from Qwen2.5-7B. Fit one score threshold on a single split and measure its accuracy and AUROC on the other, then compare with a threshold fitted on all pooled passes. Report how far scores move between passes, using the score distributions of correct responses.
CONTROLS: A threshold fitted on a single pass, a random-score baseline, rank-normalized scores before thresholding, and bootstrap resampling of 200 draws for the intervals.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Thresholds fitted on 1 pass should lose about 2 points of accuracy against pooled ones. The stability result may fail to carry over to other domains, since only math responses are scored here.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Soft-label training from annotator disagreement on Qwen2.5-7B
PROPOSAL: On HelpSteer2-Preference, which records several annotator votes per pair, train Qwen2.5-7B with a Bradley-Terry loss whose target is the vote fraction instead of a hard label, and compare with hard-label training, retraining both 3 times with different seeds, 4 epochs at learning rate 1e-5. Evaluate pairwise accuracy on RewardBench, accuracy and calibration error on held-out pairs grouped into 4 agreement buckets, and the correlation between predicted preference probability and vote fraction. Add a score-variance head and test whether its output tracks disagreement.
CONTROLS: Hard-label training, label smoothing at 0.1 with hard labels, dropping pairs with split votes, and soft labels from a random half of the votes.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Soft labels should raise the correlation with vote fraction from about 0.3 to 0.5 at equal pairwise accuracy. The variance head may fail to track disagreement if it learns to predict response length instead.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Label-noise injection study of soft targets on three backbones and three preference sets
PROPOSAL: Inject synthetic label noise at rates from 0 to 40 percent in steps of 10 into 3 preference sets: HelpSteer2-Preference, UltraFeedback and Skywork-Reward-Preference. Train Qwen2.5-1.5B, 7B and 14B with a Bradley-Terry loss on hard labels and on vote-fraction targets, with 3 runs per setting. Evaluate pairwise accuracy on RewardBench, accuracy and calibration error on held-out pairs grouped into 4 agreement buckets, and the correlation between predicted preference probability and vote fraction. Report the noise rate at which the two target types cross.
CONTROLS: Hard-label training at the same noise rates, label smoothing, dropping the pairs with split votes, and soft labels from a random half of the votes.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Soft targets should overtake hard labels beyond about 20 percent noise on the three backbones. The crossing point may fail to be stable between sets if their vote counts per pair differ.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fixed-threshold filtering of policy samples with a calibrated reward model on math and code
PROPOSAL: Draw 16 samples per problem from 3 policies, Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B, on 200 MATH-500 problems and 164 HumanEval problems. A Qwen2.5-7B reward model with calibrated absolute scores accepts a sample when its score exceeds a threshold fitted once on a 300-sample validation split. Measure precision and recall of acceptance against verified correctness, and compare the accuracy of accepted samples with Best-of-16 selection and majority voting on math.
CONTROLS: Scalar Bradley-Terry reward model with its threshold fitted likewise, a random filter at equal acceptance rate, an oracle filter from verified correctness, and thresholds fitted on 100 samples.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: The calibrated threshold should reach about 0.8 precision at 0.5 recall on math and a lower figure on code. It may fail when policies differ in solution style, so that one threshold suits only some of them.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fixed-threshold filtering with a calibrated Llama-3.1-70B reward model on grade-school math
PROPOSAL: A Llama-3.1-70B reward model whose absolute scores are anchored by 300 ratings keeps or rejects solutions that Qwen2.5-7B writes for 500 GSM8K test problems, with 64 samples per problem and the draw repeated in 5 independent draws. A sample is kept when its score passes a threshold fixed once on a 300-sample validation split; precision and recall of keeping are scored against verified correctness, and the accuracy of kept samples is compared with Best-of-64 selection and majority voting.
CONTROLS: A scalar Bradley-Terry reward model scored the same way, uniform random keeping at the same rate, an oracle keeper using verified correctness, and a threshold fixed on 100 samples.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: The calibrated threshold should reach about 0.9 precision at 0.6 recall on these problems. It may fail to carry over to harder problems, since the 500 grade-school items offer few wrong answers to learn from.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rubric-conditioned pointwise generative reward model on Qwen3-14B for three domains
PROPOSAL: Train Qwen3-14B to read a response and a short rubric, write a critique, and emit a score token from 1 to 10 for 3 epochs at learning rate 1e-5, with supervised warm-up on 20000 critiques and reinforcement learning on 50000 preference pairs for 3 domains: chat, math and code. Read the probability over score tokens as a distribution and use its entropy as confidence. Evaluate RewardBench and RM-Bench, calibration error per domain on 600 rated responses, and the accuracy of one fixed threshold, plus Best-of-8 selection on 300 prompts.
CONTROLS: A Bradley-Terry model on the same backbone and pairs, the model without the rubric, a pairwise generative judge, and a version without the supervised warm-up.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: The scorer should match the Bradley-Terry model on ranking within 1 point and cut calibration error by about 30 percent. It may fail on code, where a critique rarely detects a runtime error.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rubric and critique-length sweep for generative reward models on three backbones and five domains
PROPOSAL: Train generative reward models on 3 backbones of 8B, 14B and 32B parameters that read a response and a rubric, write a critique capped at 64, 128 or 256 tokens, and emit a score token from 1 to 10. Use supervised warm-up on 20000 critiques and reinforcement learning on 50000 pairs for 5 domains: chat, math, code, safety and role-play, with 3 runs per setting. Evaluate RewardBench and RM-Bench, calibration error per domain on 600 rated responses, the accuracy of one fixed threshold, and Best-of-8 selection on 300 prompts.
CONTROLS: Bradley-Terry models on the same backbones and pairs, models without the rubric, pairwise generative judges, and versions without the supervised warm-up.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Longer critiques should help on math and code by about 2 points and not at all on chat. The sweep may fail to separate the cap settings if most critiques end before 64 tokens anyway.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Head design comparison on Qwen2.5-1.5B with four output heads
PROPOSAL: Compare 4 output heads on Qwen2.5-1.5B trained with the Bradley-Terry loss on 20000 Skywork-Reward-Preference pairs: a linear value head, an MLP head, a categorical head over 5 levels and a Beta-distribution head with mean and concentration. Add 500 absolute ratings from HelpSteer2 for the 2 distributional heads. Evaluate pairwise accuracy on RewardBench, calibration error on 300 held-out rated responses and the agreement of predicted spread with annotator vote splits, repeating the training 3 times with different seeds.
CONTROLS: The linear head as the baseline, the distributional heads without ratings, an MLP head with twice the width, and a Beta head with a fixed concentration.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Ranking accuracy should differ by under 1 point between heads while the Beta and categorical heads cut calibration error by about 30 percent. The spread of the Beta head may fail to track vote splits if its concentration collapses to a constant.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Categorical head on Qwen2.5-14B with 5 retraining runs
PROPOSAL: Train a categorical head over 5 levels on Qwen2.5-14B with the Bradley-Terry loss on 20000 Skywork-Reward-Preference pairs and 500 absolute ratings from HelpSteer2, then retrain with 5 different seeds. Use the spread of the 5 expected levels as confidence, and plot that spread against the annotator vote splits for the held-out pairs. Evaluate pairwise accuracy on RewardBench, calibration error on 300 held-out rated responses and agreement of the spread with annotator vote splits.
CONTROLS: A linear head on the same backbone and pairs, the categorical head without ratings, a single-seed run of the same head, and a head with 3 levels.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Seed spread should correlate with vote splits at about 0.3, and ranking accuracy should rise by about 1 point over a single run. The spread may fail to reflect annotator disagreement if it mostly reflects optimization noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Anchoring a reward model to absolute safety ratings on Qwen2.5-14B
PROPOSAL: Adapt Qwen2.5-14B, trained for helpfulness ranking, to chatbot safety with 800 absolute safety ratings on a 1 to 5 scale and 5000 safety preference pairs. Combine the Bradley-Terry loss with a distributional rating loss, and keep ranking by adding a replay term on 5000 helpfulness pairs. Evaluate the RewardBench safety subset, XSTest refusal accuracy, calibration error on 400 held-out rated responses and the accuracy of one fixed threshold, retraining 3 times and reporting 95 percent bootstrap intervals.
CONTROLS: The unadapted model, training on safety pairs only, a version with the rating loss only, and a version with 200 ratings instead of 800.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Calibration error should fall by about 40 percent and the helpfulness ranking accuracy should drop by under 1 point. The anchoring may fail on borderline prompts, where the safety ratings disagree with each other.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Anchoring reward models to absolute ratings in four domains with five rating budgets
PROPOSAL: Adapt Qwen2.5-14B, trained for helpfulness ranking, to 4 domains: safety, role-play, code and math, with absolute ratings on a 1 to 5 scale at 5 budgets of 100, 200, 400, 800 and 1600 per domain. Combine the Bradley-Terry loss with a distributional rating loss, and keep ranking by adding a replay term on 5000 helpfulness pairs. Evaluate the RewardBench subsets, XSTest, calibration error on 400 held-out rated responses and the accuracy of one fixed threshold, retraining 3 times per setting.
CONTROLS: The unadapted model, training on domain pairs only, a version with the rating loss only, and a version trained on pooled ratings from all 4 domains.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Calibration error should reach its floor near 400 ratings per domain, with ranking accuracy dropping under 1 point. The curve may fail to flatten in math, where absolute quality is hard to rate by annotators.
